bull.b: FDA alignment on frataxin as a novel surrogate endpoint and acceptance of a rolling BLA create a defined regulatory path for nomlabofusp. Completing the package as planned could shorten the route from development to potential accelerated approval and commercialization.

Longer-term data showing generally manageable safety across more than 10,000 doses and sustained frataxin increases strengthen the lead program’s clinical foundation. Directional improvements in outcome measures also support continued development and potential differentiation in Friedreich’s ataxia.

Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $156.3 million, with runway projected into the third quarter of 2027, provide funding visibility through planned Phase 3 work. This supports execution of regulatory and launch preparations before near-term financing becomes necessary.

bear.b: Zero revenue across multiple reporting periods confirms that Larimar remains dependent on clinical development rather than an established commercial product. Until nomlabofusp is approved and launched, the business lacks recurring operating revenue to offset research, regulatory and launch expenditures.

Losses have expanded materially as Larimar advances its lead program and prepares for potential commercialization, raising the scale of ongoing funding requirements. Persistent negative earnings reduce financial self-sufficiency and leave results highly dependent on clinical and regulatory execution.

Accelerating operating cash outflows indicate that development and commercial-readiness spending is consuming capital at a rising rate. Even with current liquidity, deeply negative free cash flow means future financing or other capital sources may remain important as Phase 3 and launch activities progress.
